Grateful Dead, Aoxomoxoa, album cover

Rick Griffin’s cover for the Grateful Dead’s third album, 1969, adapted from a concert-poster painting, with the band name in large flowing capitals.

Context

Aoxomoxoa is the Grateful Dead’s third studio album, released on 20 June 1969 by Warner Bros.-Seven Arts. The title is a palindrome made up by the cover artist Rick Griffin and the lyricist Robert Hunter. Wikipedia.

According to Wikipedia, the artwork is adapted from a painting first made as a concert poster for the band. The bottom shows death, rebirth, and the cycle of life, with fertility symbols and Egyptian-based imagery; the top shows a sun that doubles as an egg; stylized censers stand at both sides. The words “Grateful Dead” are written in large, flowing capital letters. Wikipedia.

Rolling Stone ranked it eighth among the best album covers of all time in 1991, as cited by Wikipedia. Griffin also designed the Flying Eyeball poster. Wikipedia: Rick Griffin.

Why it belongs

The sleeve documents how the poster artists moved into album packaging, which carried the style far beyond San Francisco.

What to review next
